Compare Gaussian GARCH specifications, one-day VaR exceedances, and approximate capital reserves across forecast horizons.

## Scope

Results describe the supplied historical snapshot or a stated simulation. Model fit and scenario estimates are not evidence of performance on new observations. See the project README for the execution record and limitations.

```{r}
source("R/analytics_support.R")
set.seed(42)
```

```{r}
# Tickers for the seven ETFs chosen in portfolio specification
tickers <- c("VTI", "VEA", "VWO", "BND", "VNQ", "GLD", "QQQ")

# Portfolio weight on each ticker, matching the order above
weights <- c(0.35, 0.15, 0.10, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05, 0.10)

# Confirm weights sum to one
stopifnot(abs(sum(weights) - 1) < 1e-8)

# Total portfolio market value, used to convert return-based risk measures
# into dollar terms for the Board's capital reserve
portf.value <- 500e6
```

```{r}
date_start <- "2020-01-01"        # first calendar date of the full sample
date_end   <- "2025-03-15"        # pulled past 30 trading days into 2025 as a buffer
ntickers   <- length(tickers)     # number of assets to loop over

for (i in 1:ntickers) {
  # Load adjusted price history for the requested ticker
  px  <- read_market_history(tickers[i], 
                    from = date_start, to = date_end)
  px  <- Ad(px)                              # keep the adjusted close column only
  ret <- na.omit(diff(px) / lag(px)) # daily discrete (simple) returns
  if (i == 1) {
    data <- ret                              # first ticker seeds the data object
  } else {
    data <- merge(data, ret)                 # later tickers are joined on by date
  }
}
names(data)     <- tickers        # label columns with their ticker symbols
data            <- na.omit(data)  # drop the leading NA row from the return calc
print(range(index(data)))         # confirms the actual date range pulled
matret_discrete <- as.matrix(data) # store aligned returns as a plain numeric matrix

# Portfolio discrete return, then convert to log return
# weighted_returns() does a matrix multiply that strips the xts class off,
# so we re-attach the date index right away to keep everything downstream
# (index(), rbind(), ugarchfit()) behaving like a proper time series
portf.DiscreteRet <- weighted_returns(matret_discrete, weights, discrete = TRUE)
portf.DiscreteRet <- xts(portf.DiscreteRet, order.by = index(data))
portf.LogRet       <- log(1 + portf.DiscreteRet)

# Split into training (2020-2024) and test (first 30 trading days of 2025)
# NOTE: use index(data), not index(portf.LogRet) - weighted_returns() does a
# matrix multiply that strips the xts date index off the return vectors
dates        <- index(data)
train.idx    <- dates <= calendar_date(2024,12,31)
train.logret <- portf.LogRet[train.idx]
test.logret  <- head(portf.LogRet[!train.idx], 30)

# Combined series used later for rolling backtesting over the test window
full.logret <- rbind(train.logret, test.logret)

n.train <- length(train.logret)
n.test  <- length(test.logret)
n.train
n.test
```

```{r}
train.vec <- as.numeric(train.logret)

# Histogram of training log returns vs. a fitted Normal density
normal_fit_plot(train.vec)
```

```{r}
# Summary moments of the training log returns
r.mean <- mean(train.vec)
r.sd   <- sd(train.vec)
r.skew <- skewness(train.vec)
r.kurt <- kurtosis(train.vec)

r.mean
r.sd
r.skew
r.kurt
```

```{r}
# ACF of raw returns: checks whether the (absent) mean specification is reasonable
acf(train.vec, main = "ACF of Daily Log Returns")
```

```{r}
# ACF of squared returns: checks for volatility clustering (ARCH effects)
acf(train.vec^2, main = "ACF of Squared Daily Log Returns")
```

```{r}
# Current model: no mean, GARCH(1,1), Gaussian innovations
spec.current <- ugarchspec(
  mean.model     = list(armaOrder = c(0,0), include.mean = FALSE),
  variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(1,1)),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

# Alt 1: vary the mean only (AR(1) with intercept), same GARCH(1,1) Normal volatility
spec.alt1 <- ugarchspec(
  mean.model     = list(armaOrder = c(1,0), include.mean = TRUE),
  variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(1,1)),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

# Alt 2: vary the volatility only (GJR-GARCH for leverage), same no-mean, Normal
spec.alt2 <- ugarchspec(
  mean.model     = list(armaOrder = c(0,0), include.mean = FALSE),
  variance.model = list(model = "gjrGARCH", garchOrder = c(1,1)),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)
```

```{r}
# Fit each spec on the training sample only
fit.current <- ugarchfit(spec.current, data = train.logret, solver = "hybrid")
fit.alt1    <- ugarchfit(spec.alt1,    data = train.logret, solver = "hybrid")
fit.alt2    <- ugarchfit(spec.alt2,    data = train.logret, solver = "hybrid")
stopifnot(convergence(fit.current) == 0, convergence(fit.alt1) == 0, convergence(fit.alt2) == 0)

# AIC for each (row "Akaike" of infocriteria)
AIC.current <- infocriteria(fit.current)["Akaike",]
AIC.alt1    <- infocriteria(fit.alt1)["Akaike",]
AIC.alt2    <- infocriteria(fit.alt2)["Akaike",]

AIC.current
AIC.alt1
AIC.alt2
```

```{r}
# Backtest the 1-day 95% VaR over the test sample with a daily refit,
# moving window equal in length to the training sample.
# ugarchroll's as.data.frame() output stores the realized return and the
# 5% VaR forecast; a violation is a day the realized return fell below VaR
count_violations <- function(spec) {
  roll <- ugarchroll(
    spec, data = full.logret,
    n.start       = n.train,
    refit.every   = 1,
    refit.window  = "moving",
    calculate.VaR = TRUE,
    VaR.alpha     = 0.05,
    solver        = "hybrid"
  )
  df <- as.data.frame(roll)
  # column names from ugarchroll: "Realized" and "alpha(5%)" hold the
  # realized return and the VaR forecast at the 5% tail
  sum(df$Realized < df[["alpha(5%)"]])
}
viol.current <- count_violations(spec.current)
viol.alt1    <- count_violations(spec.alt1)
viol.alt2    <- count_violations(spec.alt2)

viol.current
viol.alt1
viol.alt2
```

```{r}
# Standardized residuals from the training fit, and the ACF of their squares
resid.current <- residuals(fit.current, standardize = TRUE)
resid.alt1    <- residuals(fit.alt1,    standardize = TRUE)
resid.alt2    <- residuals(fit.alt2,    standardize = TRUE)

acf(as.numeric(resid.current)^2, main = "ACF of Squared Std. Residuals: Current Model")
acf(as.numeric(resid.alt1)^2,    main = "ACF of Squared Std. Residuals: Alt 1 (Mean)")
acf(as.numeric(resid.alt2)^2,    main = "ACF of Squared Std. Residuals: Alt 2 (Volatility)")
```

```{r}
# Side by side comparison of the three models
model.compare <- data.table(
  Model      = c("Current (no mean, sGARCH)", "Alt 1 (AR(1) mean, sGARCH)", "Alt 2 (no mean, gjrGARCH)"),
  AIC        = c(AIC.current, AIC.alt1, AIC.alt2),
  Violations = c(viol.current, viol.alt1, viol.alt2)
)
model.compare
```

```{r}
# Uses ugarchforecast (not simulation) to get the h-day mean and variance
# using summed forecast variances as an approximation for multi-day risk.
# This avoids the instability that came from bootstrap-resampling fat-tailed
# residuals under a highly persistent GARCH process, which was producing
# NaNs and dollar losses larger than the portfolio itself.
forecast_cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
rolling_mean_ES <- function(spec, horizon, confidence) {
  alpha   <- 1 - confidence
  z.alpha <- qnorm(alpha)

  starts <- seq(1, n.test, by = horizon)
  starts <- starts[starts + horizon - 1 <= n.test]  # keep only full windows

  es.vals <- numeric(length(starts))
  for (j in seq_along(starts)) {
    end.idx       <- n.train + starts[j] - 1          # last obs in this expanding window
    logret_window <- full.logret[1:end.idx]

    key <- paste(digest::digest(spec), end.idx, horizon, sep = "-")
    if (!exists(key, envir = forecast_cache, inherits = FALSE)) {
      fit <- ugarchfit(spec, data = logret_window, solver = "hybrid")
      stopifnot(convergence(fit) == 0)
      fc <- ugarchforecast(fit, n.ahead = horizon)
      assign(key, c(mu = sum(as.numeric(fitted(fc))),
                    sd = sqrt(sum(as.numeric(sigma(fc))^2))), envir = forecast_cache)
    }
    cached <- get(key, envir = forecast_cache)
    mu.h <- cached[["mu"]]
    sd.h <- cached[["sd"]]

    # Closed-form Normal ES: -(mean - sd * dnorm(z_alpha)/alpha), in return terms
    es.return  <- -(mu.h - sd.h * dnorm(z.alpha) / alpha)
    es.vals[j] <- portf.value * es.return
  }
  mean(es.vals, na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

```{r}
horizons     <- c(1, 5, 10)
confidences  <- c(0.99, 0.95, 0.90)
model.specs  <- list(Current = spec.current, `Alt 1` = spec.alt1, `Alt 2` = spec.alt2)

results <- data.table(expand.grid(
  Horizon    = horizons,
  Confidence = confidences
))
results[, `:=`(Current = NA_real_, `Alt 1` = NA_real_, `Alt 2` = NA_real_)]

for (i in 1:nrow(results)) {
  h     <- results$Horizon[i]
  conf  <- results$Confidence[i]
  for (m in names(model.specs)) {
    results[i, (m) := rolling_mean_ES(model.specs[[m]], h, conf)]
  }
}

# Order rows to match the comparison table layout and add a label column
results <- results[order(-Confidence, Horizon)]
results[, Label := paste0(Horizon, "-day @ ", Confidence * 100, "%")]
setcolorder(results, c("Label", "Current", "Alt 1", "Alt 2"))
results
```

## Interpretation limits

Multi-day reserves use an approximation based on summed conditional forecast variances. Future GARCH returns are not jointly Gaussian merely because one-step innovations are Gaussian. AR mean dynamics can also induce cross-period covariance. A short VaR exceedance check does not validate expected shortfall.
